patch.value: GH-1749: adding a secret-guard rule breaks typed consumers' exhaustive Record<SecretGuardFinding['rule'], ...> policy maps; offer a stable category per rule and a default-plus-overrides policy helper

GitHub issue 1749 (fleet report): extensions that type a per-rule secret guard policy as an exhaustive Record over SecretGuardFinding['rule'] failed tsc with TS2741 on the 2026.11.13 bump, when the rule union gained credential_key_assignment. The detector was additive, but for exhaustive typed consumers it is a breaking type change that the release notes did not flag. Proposed: export a stable category per rule (for example credential, identity, path, network) and a policy helper such as a default decision plus partial overrides with a decide function, so a new credential rule inherits refuse without breaking compilation; and list new rule literals under a typed-consumers note in release notes. Related: the secret-guard family pm-hw00c2 (credential-key reference literals) and pm-x07qz2 (property names) changed the same finding type.

The SDK exports a stable per-rule category map and a policy helper that decides a finding from a default plus partial overrides, typed so adding a rule never breaks a consumer that uses it; the SDK surface snapshot records the addition; release notes or the SDK migration notes call out new rule literals for exhaustive consumers; tests prove a newly added rule inherits the category default
Adding a detector does not break typed consumers on a calendar bump, or the SDK offers a supported default-plus-overrides policy
An exhaustive Record over the rule union fails TS2741 whenever a rule is added
